# Harvest Calendar Naija

> Harvest Calendar Naija is a free crop calendar for Nigeria, built by students of the ByteBusters Coding Club, Yewa College, Ilaro (Odu'a Investment Foundation), Ogun State. It shows when to plant and harvest 84 Nigerian crops in all 36 states and the FCT, checks live rain and soil moisture to say whether the rains have truly started, and has an AI Farm Doctor that explains crop diseases in 17 Nigerian languages.

Key facts:
- Nigerian rains start in the South around March-April and reach the far North around June.
- The rains have truly started when about 20 mm of rain falls within 3 days; 10+ dry days in a row after planting can kill seedlings.
- Dry-season (fadama/irrigated) crops such as wheat, onion and tomato are planted from November in the North.
- Facts are checked against IITA, NAERLS, NRCRI, NCRI, NIHORT, CRIN, NIFOR, IAR and FAO. Always confirm local dates with an ADP extension officer.
- Weather data: Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

## Tools
- [Is it time to plant?](https://harvest-calendar-naija.vercel.app/planting.html): live rain, soil and dry-spell check for any state and crop
- [Farm Doctor](https://harvest-calendar-naija.vercel.app/doctor.html): describe a sick plant, get likely causes and safe steps
- [12-month crop chart](https://harvest-calendar-naija.vercel.app/calendar.html)
